name: Orchards (mango, citrus, dates, apples)

problems.words: Gave the orchard on theka and the thekedar paid only half
quick_ideas: Write down what has been received and what remains, so the conversation starts from facts
Send the thekedar that summary politely in writing; for the contract itself, talk to your lawyer.

workzap_build.text: A theka tracker holding every orchard's instalments, sending WhatsApp reminders before each due date and showing what is overdue at a glance.

problems.ask_first: Were the instalment dates written in the agreement?
problems.free_stops: How instalments and reminders are set up for your theka deals goes in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the orchard handover notes, harvest timing and payments received in one page, so you can see exactly what is still unsettled.
Give one person the job of keeping every theka payment note in one envelope, so follow up starts from one agreed record.

problems.words: I don't know if theka is better or picking myself
quick_ideas: Put last season's theka amount for each block next to what any self-picked block earned after costs, to get a first comparison
Note this season's costs by block from the start.

workzap_build.text: An orchard register by block that records picks, sales and costs every season, so theka and own-picking compare side by side automatically.

problems.ask_first: Have you picked any block yourself in the last two seasons?
problems.free_stops: Which costs are counted and how the comparison is built stays in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note one block sold on theka beside one similar block picked by your own team, so the earning difference is clearer.
Give one person one page per block for all picking and sale notes, so season comparisons stop relying on scattered memory.

problems.words: Pickers are paid per crate and the counts get disputed
quick_ideas: Show each picker their count before they leave, so disagreements are settled the same day
Have the supervisor note counts at set times rather than only at day end.

workzap_build.text: A picking tally on phone recording crates per picker number per day with the supervisor's count, producing the pay sheet automatically.

problems.ask_first: Who counts the crates during picking now?
problems.free_stops: The tally and pay sheet setup is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count crates at the loading point and compare them with the picker tally once that day, so the mismatch size shows early.
Give one supervisor the crate count notebook for the whole shift, so picker pay talks start from one running total.

problems.words: We ran out of crates in the middle of picking
quick_ideas: Count crates and cartons on hand now, before the season, so there are no surprises
Check last season's dispatches to see roughly how many you got through.

workzap_build.text: A crate and packing material tracker that alerts you before stock falls below what the coming weeks of picking need.

problems.ask_first: Do you pack yourself or does the buyer bring crates?
problems.free_stops: Reorder levels and how usage is tracked go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk the storage area and count empty and usable crates separately today, so you know how short the next picking day may be.
Give one store hand the job of noting crates issued and returned in one place, so field teams stop pulling from hidden piles.

problems.words: Too many crates arrive bruised by the time they reach Lahore / Karachi
quick_ideas: Ask buyers to send a photo and count on arrival, so damage is tied to a specific truck
Note which transporter and route had the most complaints.

workzap_build.text: A dispatch register for every truck with the buyer's arrival count and photos, showing route by route where damage happens.

problems.ask_first: Do you arrange transport or does the buyer?
problems.free_stops: How dispatches and arrival checks are linked is part of the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note bruising complaints by truck, route and orchard lot for this week's arrivals, so the roughest movement pattern stands out.
Give one person the arrival complaint notebook for every load, so transporter follow up is based on one season record.

problems.words: Fruit sold in the mandi at a rate I never get to see on paper
quick_ideas: Ask the arhti for a slip per lot showing rate, weight and deductions, so every sale has a record
Keep those slips in one place for the season.

workzap_build.text: A mandi sale reconciliation that sets each dispatch against the rate received and deductions, line by line, every day.

problems.ask_first: Do you sell through one arhti or several?
problems.free_stops: How slips are reconciled against dispatches is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the lots sent to the mandi with the sale slips received this week, so missing paper for any sale stands out.
Give one person one folder for every mandi slip and deduction note, so your season record stays together for review.

problems.words: Grading is different every day depending on who is on the line
quick_ideas: Put sample photos of each grade where grading happens, so everyone works to the same picture
Note each buyer complaint against the date and line.

workzap_build.text: A grading log by day and line with photo checks, linking buyer complaints back to the dispatch they came from.

problems.ask_first: Do you grade yourself, or does a packing house?
problems.free_stops: The grading log design is part of the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Lay out one day's graded fruit by grade and compare it with the next shift's output, so the grading drift is easier to spot.
Give one line leader the job of keeping disputed grades in one tray until review, so daily grading calls stay more consistent.

problems.words: My UAE date farm is run by a manager and I only see totals
quick_ideas: Ask the manager for one daily message with weights, deliveries, workers and spend, so you see more than totals
Go through it together weekly, as routine rather than suspicion.

workzap_build.text: A daily read for owners abroad showing weights, deliveries, labour and spend from the manager's entries, with the one thing to look at.

problems.ask_first: How often are you at the farm during the season?
problems.free_stops: What goes into the daily read and how it is fed is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the daily totals with separate notes on loads, worker turnout and spending for one week, so weak reporting areas show quickly.
Give the manager one fixed time to send one daily orchard summary, so you see movement in the farm not only totals.

problems.words: Corporate gift orders for dates in Ramadan pile up on WhatsApp
quick_ideas: Copy every gift order into one sheet the day it arrives, so nothing lives only in a chat
Confirm each order back to the customer before packing.

workzap_build.text: One place for WhatsApp and online gift orders, each tracked from confirmation to delivery.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many gift orders come in a busy week?
problems.free_stops: How orders are captured and tracked is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many gift orders in recent chats lack a packing note or delivery note, so the backlog size is clear.
Give one staff member one notebook for every incoming gift order that day, so packing work stops getting lost in busy chats.

problems.words: Repeat buyers from last year never hear from us again
quick_ideas: List last season's direct buyers who agreed to hear from you, so you have a starting list
Reach out with their permission when the new crop is near.

workzap_build.text: A customer list of past buyers who gave permission, with pre-season WhatsApp messages sent on time each year.

problems.ask_first: Do you sell any fruit directly to households or offices?
problems.free_stops: Message timing and wording are part of the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many direct buyers from last season you can still identify from old slips and chats, so the missed repeat business shows.
Give one staff member one notebook for buyer follow ups every market day, so returning buyers hear when the crop is ready.

never_say: Anything on sprays, fertilisers, pruning, doses, fruit fly or disease control, ripening chemicals or post-harvest treatments; refer to an agronomist, extension office or plant-protection authority.
Advice on phytosanitary rules, export regulations or certificates.
Legal views on theka contracts or thekedar disputes.
Any help with banned ripening chemicals, mislabelling origin, faking certificates or under-invoicing exports.
Seasonal worker visa or programme advice, or accusations against a manager or caretaker.

sample_reply.person: Thekedar ka masla phir se na ho, koi solution do. Is saal bhi bagh theke pe dena hai.
sample_reply.pi:
Bilkul, ye masla hal ho sakta hai, aur pehla qadam aasan hai.
Pehle, pichle theke ki wasool shuda aur baqi raqam ek safhe pe likh kar thekedar ko tehreeri tor pe bhej dein, taake baat hisaab se shuru ho.
Doosra, naye theke mein har qist ki tareekh saaf likhwayein, aur qanooni pehlu apne wakeel se dekh lein.
Workzap aap ke liye ye rakh sakta hai: har qist ka hisaab, tareekh se pehle WhatsApp yaad-dihani, aur baqi raqam ek nazar mein.

Kya main aap ke liye solution document aur quote banwa doon? Mana bhi kar sakte hain.
